title: Podcast feed tokens authorize every episode, not just the token owner's episodes

evidence.quote:
prefs = podcast_service.get_preferences_by_feed_token(session, token)
    if prefs is None:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="Invalid feed token")
    if not prefs.podcast_feed_enabled:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Podcast feed is disabled")

    base_url = _podcast_base_url(request, prefs.podcast_feed_base_url)
    episodes = session.exec(
        select(PodcastEpisode)
        .where(PodcastEpisode.status == "ready")

reasoning: A valid private podcast feed token is only checked for existence, then stream/download fetches the requested episode by ID with no owner or preference scope check. The RSS feed query similarly returns all ready episodes. In any multi-user deployment, one user's feed token can enumerate or download another user's ready podcast episodes.
reproduction: Create two users with podcast preferences and ready episodes. Use user B's podcast feed token to request `/api/podcast/episodes/{user_A_episode_id}/download?token={user_B_token}` or `/api/podcast/feed.xml?token={user_B_token}`; the code authorizes the token and does not filter by user.
recommendation: Have `_authorize_standard_or_feed_token` return the matched preferences/user identity, and require `PodcastEpisode.user_id == prefs.user_id` for feed XML, stream, download, and artwork-derived episode links. Return 404 for episodes outside the token scope.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked tests only cover feeds, health/config covers, and KOReader plugin packaging; none exercise podcast feed-token authorization or multi-user isolation.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a podcast API test with two users, two feed tokens, and an episode owned by user A; assert user B's feed token cannot see or download user A's episode.
minimumFixScope: app/api/podcast.py authorization helper plus the feed XML, stream, and download handlers.

history.reasoning: The original path app/api/podcast.py still exists, but the cited evidence has changed. _authorize_standard_or_feed_token now returns the resolved PodcastPreferences for feed tokens at lines 242-262 instead of returning None. stream_podcast_episode now rejects feed-token access when episode.user_id != token_prefs.user_id at lines 641-648, and download_podcast_episode has the same owner check at lines 697-704. get_podcast_feed_xml now filters ready episodes with PodcastEpisode.user_id == prefs.user_id at lines 737-741. A regression test exists at tests/test_podcast_api.py:437-517 and asserts a second user's feed token cannot see, download, or stream the first user's episode while still allowing its own episode. I did not find another feed-token episode access path in app/api/podcast.py. I attempted to run the focused pytest, but the read-only sandbox has no writable temporary directory, so pytest could not start; the code and test source indicate this finding is fixed.
